result.summary: Removes trailing newline escape sequences from single-line log function calls across the codebase using a scripted diff. It targets LogDebug, LogError, LogInfo, LogTrace, and LogWarning invocations whose format strings do not contain quotes or backslashes.
result.problem: Log message format strings sometimes end with a trailing newline character. Although the logging framework strips a single trailing newline, keeping them creates confusing inconsistencies with logging rules that escape embedded newlines, risks bugs when multiple trailing newlines are present, and falsely implies that explicit newline formatting is supported.
evidence: PR description: 'After #35833 embedded newlines are escaped and a single trailing one is excluded. It would be clearer to not have a special carve-out here. Also the carve-out may be missing two-or-more trailing newlines.'
result.scope_notes: Mechanical scripted-diff touching 63 files, executed via a single sed command provided in the commit message.
result.card: Executes a scripted diff removing trailing newline escape sequences from single-line log messages across 63 files. Log functions currently strip single trailing newlines, but their presence creates special carve-outs and implies newline formatting is supported. The author notes that after PR 35833 escaped embedded newlines, removing trailing newlines avoids special-case handling and edge cases with multiple trailing newlines. There are no prerequisites.

risk.why: This is a purely mechanical cleanup of logging format strings with no effect on node behavior or consensus.
